title: API 570 Training in Houston: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: API 570 exam prep online for Houston piping inspectors: CUI, CML programmes, injection points, dead legs and B31.3, self-paced with instructor Q&A.
h1: API 570 Training in Houston: Self-Paced Exam Prep for Process and Unit Piping Inspectors
html:
API 570 exam prep for piping inspectors in Houston

Walk any unit along the Houston Ship Channel and most of what you pass is pipe: transfer lines, overhead lines, pump suction and discharge piping, steam and condensate, flare headers and the racks that carry them to tank farms and docks. API 570 is the in-service inspection code for that piping, and the API 570 Piping Inspector certification is what owner-users and inspection contractors around Houston ask for when they want someone to set circuits, judge thickness data and approve repairs.

This page covers how a candidate in Pasadena, Deer Park, Baytown, Texas City or anywhere else in the region prepares with the Atlantis course. It is self-paced online study with an instructor who answers your questions, so it fits around rotating shifts and turnaround work. There is no Atlantis classroom in Houston. API sets eligibility, administers the API 570 examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification, and each candidate applies to API on their own.

Piping-heavy sites along the Ship Channel

Refinery and chemical plant piping is the obvious starting point, but Houston has an unusual amount of terminal and dock piping as well, and those manifolds are API 570 territory too. Kinder Morgan's own terminal sheets show the scale. Its Pasadena terminal lists 22 inbound and 18 outbound pipelines, including connections to the Colonial and Explorer pipelines, and its Galena Park terminal on the opposite bank lists 12 inbound and 10 outbound lines plus nine marine docks. Sixteen cross-channel pipelines connect the Pasadena site with Galena Park, the Kinder Morgan Export Terminal and the North Docks.

ONEOK's Galena Park marine terminal, which came with the Magellan business, sends product out through the Colonial, Explorer and Magellan south system pipelines and loads ships, barges, rail cars and trucks. Colonial's own system, about 5,500 miles of pipe in all, starts in Houston and ends in Linden, New Jersey. Downstream of the refineries, Enterprise announced in 2024 an expansion at its Enterprise Hydrocarbons Terminal on the channel designed to add roughly 300,000 barrels a day of propane and butane export capability, with service expected by the end of 2026, and LPG loading piping brings the low-temperature and impact-test questions in the Body of Knowledge to life.

Inside the fence lines, the ExxonMobil Baytown complex, the Shell Deer Park Chemicals plant and Chevron Phillips Chemical's Cedar Bayou plant each run piping systems large enough to keep a dedicated piping inspection group busy. API 570 is written for in-service process piping like this; cross-country transmission pipelines fall under federal pipeline rules and are a different discipline.

Corrosion under insulation, the Houston piping inspector's constant

Houston's humid subtropical weather, salt-laden air near the bay and frequent heavy rain keep insulation wet for long periods, so corrosion under insulation dominates many piping inspection plans in the region. The current API 570 Body of Knowledge reflects that: corrosion under insulation, chloride stress corrosion cracking and atmospheric corrosion are all among the fifteen API RP 571 mechanisms it lists, together with soil corrosion, sour water corrosion, hydrochloric acid corrosion, sulfidation, caustic corrosion, caustic stress corrosion cracking, amine stress corrosion cracking, erosion/erosion-corrosion, galvanic corrosion, MIC, mechanical fatigue (including vibration-induced fatigue) and boiler water and steam condensate corrosion.

In the field, CUI concentrates where water gets in and stays: damaged jacketing and seals, insulation terminations at flanges and valves, pipe supports and trunnions, low points, vertical runs that collect water at the bottom, steam-traced lines and lines that cycle through the temperature range where wet carbon steel corrodes fastest. Austenitic stainless lines under the same insulation can crack instead of thinning. For the exam, learn what RP 571 says about susceptible materials and temperatures, and what API 570 recommends for the extent of CUI inspection by piping class. The CUI glossary entry and the API RP 583 summary cover the working detail. AMPP, the corrosion and coatings association formed in 2021 from NACE International and SSPC, has offices in Houston, which is one reason so much CUI practice is discussed locally.

CML programmes, injection points and dead legs

Houston plants organise their piping into circuits of similar material and service, place condition monitoring locations (CMLs) where thinning is expected, and track every reading in an inspection data management system. An API 570 inspector reviews that history, decides whether the CMLs still sit in the right places and sets the next thickness and external visual inspection dates. The 570 examination tests the same chain of judgement.

  • Injection points. Wash water upstream of overhead condensers, caustic or ammonia for neutralisation and corrosion inhibitors are injected all over the region's units. API 570 lets an injection point be treated as its own inspection circuit, recommends how far that circuit extends upstream and downstream, and gives it an inspection frequency of its own rather than the surrounding piping's. Expect questions on where the circuit starts and ends and why.
  • Dead legs. Bypasses, standby pump lines, drains and capped branches collect water and sludge while flow passes them by. Inspectors look at both the stagnant end and the junction with the active line, and the code encourages removing dead legs that serve no purpose.
  • Soil-to-air interfaces. Dock, terminal and tank-farm lines that dive underground at road crossings corrode just above and below grade.
  • Small-bore and auxiliary piping. Instrument connections, vents and sample points vibrate and are easy to leave out of a CML plan; mechanical and vibration-induced fatigue is on the mechanism list for that reason.
  • Mixing points and high-velocity zones. Where streams of different temperature or composition meet, or flow is turbulent past elbows and tees, erosion and localised corrosion follow.

A worked corrosion rate and interval example

The Body of Knowledge says the corrosion rate, remaining life and interval rules (API 570 7.1.2, 7.2, 6.3.3 and Table 1) may be examined closed-book, so work them until they are automatic. Consider a hypothetical 8 in. carbon steel dock line at a Galena Park terminal with a baseline reading of 0.322 in. twenty years ago, 0.282 in. four years ago and 0.262 in. now, and a minimum required thickness of 0.200 in. supplied by the engineer.

  1. Long-term rate: (0.322 − 0.262) / 20 = 0.003 in. per year.
  2. Short-term rate: (0.282 − 0.262) / 4 = 0.005 in. per year.
  3. Compare the two. The recent readings show faster loss, so the short-term rate better reflects current service, and the inspector should be able to justify whichever rate is used.
  4. Remaining life at 0.005 in. per year: (0.262 − 0.200) / 0.005 = 12.4 years.
  5. Next thickness inspection: half the remaining life, 6.2 years, unless the maximum for the line's piping class in API 570's interval table is shorter.

Pressure design thickness for the same line comes from ASME B31.3 304.1.2, t = PD / [2(SEW + PY)]. With an outside diameter of 8.625 in., 285 psig, S given as 20,000 psi, E and W of 1.0 and Y of 0.4, t = 2,458 / 40,228 = 0.061 in. That figure is far below the engineer's 0.200 in. because a structural or owner-set minimum usually governs low-pressure piping of this size, and the question often tests whether you know which number to use.

B31.3, B16.5 and PCC-2 in the open-book half

The effectivity sheet API published for the February and June 2027 API 570 windows lists API 570 5th edition, API RP 574 with its addendum, RP 576 sections 5, 6.1 to 6.5 and 7, RP 577, RP 578, ASME B31.3 2024 edition, B16.5 2020 edition, PCC-2 2022 and Sections V and IX of the 2023 Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code. Study the edition on the sheet for your window, because clause numbers move between editions.

  • ASME B31.3: pressure design thickness and permanent blanks, leak-test pressure for hydrostatic and pneumatic tests (345.4 and 345.5), impact-test exemptions and Charpy values (323.2.2 and 323.3), preheat and heat treatment, joint and casting quality factors, and total thermal expansion from Appendix C.
  • ASME B16.5: working pressure of a flange for a given material and temperature, the maximum temperature for a given pressure, and minimum flange dimensions. Houston plants carry a great deal of Class 150 and 300 carbon steel, but the exam can pick any rating group.
  • ASME PCC-2: the listed articles include full-encirclement sleeves, fillet-welded patches, in-service welding, flaw excavation and weld repair, flange repair and mechanical clamps. Those are the repairs Ship Channel crews make on leaking lines between turnarounds, so connect each article to a repair you have seen.

For an overview of the piping code itself, read the API 570 summary and the API RP 574 summary.

Routes into API 570 from Houston jobs

API 570 uses the same education and experience scale as API 510 and API 653, with the experience in piping: one year of inspection activity with an engineering or technology degree, up to five or more years with no formal education, gained in the last ten years while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency. The API 570 certification requirements page sets out the full table.

  • UT thickness technicians. This is a common starting point in Houston, taking CML readings on refinery and terminal piping for contractors. The experience counts when the work is inspection as API 570 describes it, so record which circuits you surveyed and who reviewed the data.
  • Inspection data technicians. People who load readings into the inspection database and flag high corrosion rates learn the code's logic early, though they still need documented inspection time.
  • Pipefitters and welders from repair crews bring construction and repair experience on piping; the two-year and high school routes include it alongside one year of inspection.
  • College graduates. San Jacinto College's Fixed Equipment Inspection Technology degree includes a course in pressure piping and valve inspection, and Lone Star College runs an inspection technology programme at its North Harris campus and East Aldine Center.
  • Engineers at owner-users and engineering firms with a bachelor's degree need one year of piping inspection activity.

ASNT NDT training for technicians who want to move into thickness survey and weld inspection work is on the Houston NDT training page.

Fitting API 570 study around Houston piping work

Use the piping you know. Take an isometric drawing from your own unit and mark the circuit boundaries, the CMLs, any injection point circuit and the dead legs, then check each decision against API 570 and RP 574. When the drawing and the code disagree, write down the question and send it to the instructor, who answers from the code text rather than from any one site's practice.

Self-paced study also lets you match the work calendar. One workable pattern is to read API 570 and RP 574 during normal weeks, leave B16.5 and B31.3 table work for days off when they can sit with the PDFs for hours, and stop almost completely when a turnaround starts. Timed practice papers are most useful in the final stretch before your window, when you need to know how long an open-book flange or test-pressure question really takes you.

Exam day and employer sponsorship

The API 570 day has 170 questions over about 7.5 hours: a short tutorial, a closed-book session, a lunch break and an open-book session with the code PDFs on screen. Prometric lists test centres in and around Houston, and you choose one when you book after API approves your application. Windows and deadlines are on the API exam schedule post.

Refineries, chemical plants, terminals and inspection contractors can enrol several piping candidates together, and a group can include people preparing for API 510 or API 653 at the same time. Fees are quoted on request. Each candidate keeps their own pace and their own questions for the instructor, and the employer's main job is accurate, signed experience records.

faq.q: Does API 570 cover the pipelines that start in Houston?
faq.a: Generally not. API 570 is written for in-service process piping in refineries, chemical plants and similar facilities, including terminal and dock piping inside those sites. Cross-country transmission pipelines such as Colonial or Explorer are regulated under federal pipeline safety rules and inspected to other standards. Read API 570's scope section for the exact inclusions and optional exclusions, because scope questions can appear on the exam.

faq.q: Is corrosion under insulation on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Yes. Corrosion under insulation is one of the API RP 571 mechanisms listed in the current API 570 Body of Knowledge, as are chloride stress corrosion cracking and atmospheric corrosion. Expect questions on susceptible materials, temperature ranges, appearance, where to look and how to inspect. API 570 and RP 574 add the inspection-planning side, such as which locations to examine and how much insulation to remove.

faq.q: Can a UT thickness technician in Houston qualify for API 570?
faq.a: Often, yes, if the thickness work counts as performing inspection activities on piping as API 570 describes them and was done for an employer or contractor that qualifies as an authorized inspection agency. The years required depend on your education: one with an engineering or technology degree, two with a two-year degree, three with high school and five or more without. API verifies the experience you document.

faq.q: Which B31.3 calculations should I practise for API 570?
faq.a: The Body of Knowledge lists pressure design thickness of straight pipe (304.1.1 and 304.1.2), permanent blank thickness (304.5.3), hydrostatic and pneumatic leak-test pressure (345.4 and 345.5), impact-test exemption temperatures and Charpy values (323.2.2 and 323.3), preheat (330 and Table 330.1.1), joint and casting quality factors and thermal expansion from Appendix C. Add the API 570 MAWP of corroded pipe.

faq.q: Are injection points and dead legs really tested?
faq.a: Yes, and they are worth learning precisely. API 570 lets injection points be treated as separate circuits, recommends their extent upstream and downstream and gives them their own inspection frequency, and it treats dead legs as locations needing specific attention. RP 574 adds practical guidance on both. Houston candidates who have walked overhead systems with wash water or caustic injection usually find these questions easier once the code wording is familiar.

faq.q: Do I need to memorise ASME B16.5 flange ratings?
faq.a: No. Flange questions sit in the open-book half, where B16.5 is on the screen, so the skill is finding the right rating table for the material group, reading across to the temperature and interpolating where needed. Practise that speed with timed papers. You should still know closed-book what a flange class means and how pressure ratings fall as temperature rises.

faq.q: Can a Pasadena terminal or Baytown plant enrol a piping inspection group?
faq.a: Yes. Owner-users, terminal operators and inspection contractors can enrol several API 570 candidates together, alongside candidates for other API exams if needed. Fees are quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API individually with their own experience record, and studies on their own schedule with access to the instructor. Mention your target windows and turnaround dates when you enquire.

faq.q: Where do Houston candidates sit the API 570 exam?
faq.a: At a Prometric test centre. After API accepts your application you book a seat through Prometric, which lists centres in and around Houston, and you choose a date inside your window. The exam is computer-based, closed-book first and open-book after the lunch break, when the code PDFs are provided on the computer. Personal books, notes and papers are not allowed.
